rule_level_problems.rule: Urgent: diabetes with low or high fingerprick glucose
rule_level_problems.problem: The page's middle branch, 'fingerprick glucose >= 11.1 with symptoms -> 19', has no clause. The rule escalates >= 11.1 only when Ketonuria is present. The outcome is covered indirectly only if 'symptoms' means the red-box list (in which case rule 1 already fires); nothing in the file states that reading, and a symptomatic hyperglycaemic patient without ketones is otherwise not escalated.

Every due_to anchors on (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Diabetes mellitus" "disorder")). The briefing says a known chronic condition in a due_to is (active_condition ...), with the clinical_finding + 'Known present' qualifier form in a check_for. If the system records a patient's diabetes as an active condition, these rules may never fire for the very patients the page is about. Could not verify which form the system matches from the permitted inputs.

rule_level_problems.problem: Observable choices for routine vitals: pulse is (snomed_concept "Pulse, function" "observable entity") rather than "Heart rate", and glucose is "Blood glucose status" (a 'General clinical state' observable, no children) rather than "Blood glucose concentration". If the routine vitals are recorded under different observables, the pulse >= 100, glucose < 4 and glucose >= 11.1 comparisons never match. Needs checking against what the system records.

rule_level_problems.problem: The page asks for the ketone dipstick only when glucose >= 11.1 is WITHOUT symptoms; the task fires for all >= 11.1. Over-checks rather than misses; symptomatic patients are already Urgent.

rule_level_problems.rule: Measure waist circumference in routine diabetes care
rule_level_problems.problem: The page also asks for weight every visit; kg is an available unit and weight is not in the briefing's routine-vitals list, yet no measure task exists. BMI and WHR are not representable.

The page groups dry mouth, poor skin turgor, BP < 90/60 and pulse >= 100 under 'Dehydration'; the rule makes each one an independent Urgent trigger, so a diabetic with pulse 100 and nothing else is Urgent. This is the broadest defensible reading of 'any of' and matches how the gold standard treats BP < 90/60, but a clinician should confirm it.

No defect: every one of the 20 check_for findings is consumed by the danger-signs priority rule, and Ketonuria by the glucose rule; temperature, BP and pulse are routine vitals and correctly omitted from check_for. Concept choices with closer alternatives (Hungry vs Increased appetite; Asthenia vs Weakness present) are judgement calls, not errors.

summary: The red box is encoded almost completely: all 15 danger-sign criteria (23 parts) have the right concepts, thresholds and directions, and the ketone check and ketones-present escalation are correct. The one substantive gap is the page's 'glucose >= 11.1 with symptoms -> page 19' branch, which has no clause of its own and is covered only by an unstated assumption that 'symptoms' equals the red-box list. Two anchoring risks could stop the rules firing at all: the diabetes trigger is a clinical_finding rather than the active_condition form the briefing prescribes, and the pulse and glucose observables ('Pulse, function', 'Blood glucose status') may not be the ones the system records for routine vitals. The routine-care table is management and cross-references, judged out of scope, except that a weight measure task is missing alongside the waist-circumference one.
